title: Failed database commit leaves orphaned cover files
reasoning: The normalized image is written to disk before the ManualCover row is committed. If session.add/commit/refresh fails after the write, the file remains under manual_covers without a database record, so it cannot be listed, activated, or deleted through the API and will accumulate until manually cleaned up.
reproduction: Force session.commit() to raise after target_path.write_bytes succeeds; the generated file remains on disk with no corresponding ManualCover row.
recommendation: Wrap the file write and database commit in error handling that unlinks the newly written file on any failure after the write. For stronger consistency, write to a temporary path, commit the row only after a successful final rename, and clean up temp/final files in except blocks.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The manual-cover test covers a successful upload/activate/delete flow only; it does not simulate filesystem or database failures during upload.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that monkeypatches session.commit to raise after a successful write and asserts the generated manual cover file is removed.
minimumFixScope: app/api/config.py upload_manual_cover error handling around write_bytes and session.commit.
